Text of a police oversight report

Source: R/ovr.R
ovrtxt.Rd

Turns the page of a report published by a police oversight body (a civilian investigation unit, an ombudsman, an inspector) into the plain text its other tools read: markup removed, each paragraph, heading, list item and table row on a line of its own, so that section headings stand alone, and character entities decoded. Use it to read or search saved reports without a browser, or before the rules that code them.

Usage

ovrtxt(x, html = NA)

Arguments

x

The pages or texts: a character vector. NA stays NA.

html

NA (the default) to read each element as HTML when it holds markup (a < followed by a letter, / or !), TRUE or FALSE to say.

Value

A character vector the length of x, in UTF-8.

Details

Scripts, styles and comments are dropped. The start and end of a block element (a paragraph, a heading, a division, a list item, a table row, a line break and the like) end a line; every other tag is a space, and the page's own line breaks are spaces, as a browser shows them. Named entities common on report pages and every numeric entity are decoded (curly quotes and dashes to their plain forms). Spaces are collapsed, lines trimmed, and at most one empty line is kept between paragraphs. Plain text (with html = FALSE, or with no markup when html = NA) is only tidied that way, its line breaks kept. Nothing is fetched and nothing is written; the pass is linear in the length of the page.

Examples

ovrtxt("<h2>The Team</h2><p>Number of investigators assigned: 3</p>")
#> [1] "The Team\n\nNumber of investigators assigned: 3"
ovrtxt("<p>WO\n#1 Interviewed</p><p>WO&nbsp;#2 Interviewed</p>")
#> [1] "WO #1 Interviewed\n\nWO #2 Interviewed"
ovrtxt("a  b\r\nc", html = FALSE)
#> [1] "a b\nc"
